title: A Bushbaby Jumps 7 Feet Straight Up, 12 Times Its Own Body Length

scenes.text: This animal is seven inches tall. It jumps seven feet.
The galago, or bushbaby, a night-time primate of Africa with huge eyes and ears like a bat's.
Its highest reliably recorded leap is 2.25 metres straight up, about twelve times its own body length.
Its leg muscles are about a quarter of its body weight. They stretch the tendons in its legs like a catapult, then let go.
Strung together, those leaps cover ten yards in seconds, and it folds its ears flat to protect them in thick bush.
In 2016, engineers copied it to build the most agile jumping robot ever made. The robot managed 78 percent of the real thing.

description:
The galago, or bushbaby, is a small African primate whose highest reliably recorded jump is 2.25 metres straight up, about twelve times its body length, powered by tendons that store energy like a catapult.
In 2016 Berkeley engineers used it as the model for Salto, the most agile jumping robot built, which reached 78 percent of the galago's vertical jumping agility.
Which animal's superpower should robots copy next?
subject: bushbaby galago
first_comment: If you could jump twelve times your height, you would clear a seven-storey building. Which animal's ability would you steal?
